task_item: A6 - retrieve Qu et al. 2026 arXiv:2601.01558 and confirm/refute its PUB rows against the primary

artefact.title: Utilizing Earth Foundation Models to Enhance the Simulation Performance of Hydrological Models with AlphaEarth Embeddings
artefact.venue_note: running head reads 'manuscript submitted to Water Resources Research' (preprint, not yet a WRR paper)

numbers_CONFIRMED_from_primary.verbatim: Although both types of static features performed similarly in-sample, with median NSE values of 0.708 for the AEF embeddings and 0.706 for the model using CAMELS attributes, their behavior differed noticeably once they were evaluated in spatial out-of-sample settings. For these more challenging conditions, the median NSE of the AEF embeddings rose to 0.612, while the model relying on CAMELS attributes reached only 0.553.
numbers_CONFIRMED_from_primary.verdict: CONFIRMED to 3 dp. The refs output's two 'secondary' rows R18/R20 are numerically correct; the 'via Heudorfer 2026' provenance can be upgraded to PRIMARY.

protocol_CORRECTION_to_the_frozen_set.severity: MATERIAL - the frozen set's metadata for R18/R20 is wrong on three axes

primary_actually_says.verbatim_basins: We used all 671 catchments from the CAMELS dataset as experimental data.
primary_actually_says.folds: five random seeds x five-fold cross-validation, 80% train / 20% spatially-held-out test per fold
primary_actually_says.verbatim_folds: Model training and evaluation were conducted using five random seeds and a five-fold cross-validation scheme across the 671 CAMELS-US basins. In each fold, 80% of the basins were used for training, and the remaining 20% were held out as spatially independent test basins.
primary_actually_says.metric_convention: basin-level NSE pooled over 5 seeds x 5 folds, then 5000x bootstrap resampling of 80% of the pooled sample, empirical CDF on a common NSE grid, median CDF across realizations (the Heudorfer et al. 2025 convention) - NOT a plain median over a fixed basin set
primary_actually_says.model: single-layer LSTM, 128 hidden, dropout 0.4, batch 256, seq_length 365

protocol_CORRECTION_to_the_frozen_set.consequence: R20=0.553 and R18=0.612 are genuine published CAMELS-US spatial-out-of-sample numbers, but they are NOT on the pinned Li-2025 PUB protocol: different basin set (671 vs 531), different test period (2010-2014 vs 1995-1999), different fold count (5 vs 10) and a bootstrap-CDF metric convention rather than a plain median. They remain in the reference set and the kill rule is still evaluated against them, but they must be annotated as PROTOCOL-MISMATCHED, not quoted as like-for-like.

why_this_paper_is_the_closest_published_.verbatim_experiment_B: To conduct this analysis, we rank all basins in the CAMELS dataset with respect to a given target basin using three similarity measures defined in Section 2.3. Based on these rankings, we construct seven training sets by selecting the top k most similar basins, where k in {100,200,300,400,500,600}, as well as a baseline using all 670 basins except the target basin.
why_this_paper_is_the_closest_published_.target_basins: 150 basins, stratified by Koppen climate zone (~25% of CAMELS)
why_this_paper_is_the_closest_published_.key_finding: AEF-similarity donor selection peaks at k=400 donors and does not improve beyond; CAMELS-attribute similarity scales more monotonically with pool size, which the authors attribute to attribute equifinality.
why_this_paper_is_the_closest_published_.note: Qu's donor selection chooses which basins to TRAIN an LSTM on. Our donor arm transfers the donor's observed discharge directly with no training. Same similarity object, different downstream consumer.
